anchor_comparisons: ORDTRANSFER-c54e0c02076da1642b64c8df has a low-confidence ordinal 4.32-5.52 band. The current case has better source-backed operating facts, but its apparent cheapness depends heavily on forward consolidated earnings, so I do not carry the full positive-anchor uplift into valuation confidence.

ORDTRANSFER-c2ec77e0538ebb9af9ce204b has a low-confidence ordinal 2.83-4.03 counter band. The current denominator mismatch, 21.86x trailing parent PE, 18.88x forward EV/EBITDA, and 1.99% forward FCF yield keep the case near the upper part of this counter band despite strong memory execution.
disagreements: A low forward PE alone is not evidence of rerating headroom when trailing and cash-based denominators point in a different direction.
Actual memory ASP improvement cannot be mechanically translated into HBM-only margin or free cash flow, and corporate AI-factory GPU guidance is not Samsung HBM customer visibility.
payload.rationale: The operating facts are positive but do not establish a clean rerating bridge. Actual memory revenue and ASP cover DS memory broadly, not HBM-only earnings. HBM4 shipment is actual, whereas AMD MI455X alignment is an MOU and NVIDIA supply is still under discussion. The low 5.59x forward PE uses a forecast consolidated denominator and conflicts with much higher trailing PE and EV/EBITDA plus a low forward FCF yield. Without period-matched HBM profit and cash attribution, the valuation signal is fragile and deserves a score close to the counter anchor rather than the optimistic headline multiple.
payload.why_not_higher: There is no HBM-specific earnings or cash denominator, the forward and trailing valuation measures are not period-comparable, forward FCF yield is only 1.99%, and named-customer HBM4 economics are not contractually disclosed.
payload.why_not_lower: Actual memory revenue and ASP expansion, actual HBM4 shipments, and AMD's official confirmation of Samsung's HBM3E role are genuine execution evidence and prevent the valuation thesis from being merely speculative.
